## Trunking

Wire `Device iq` → **Trunk system**, enter **Control** (MHz), and pick **Protocol** (or **Auto-detect**) and **Decoder** (DMR, P25 Phase 1, or MPT 1327). Runs server-side with no browser open; voice grants must fit inside the Device's window.

```patch
[source] Device : Radio
[tool] Trunk system : Control channel
[output] Speaker : Voice
[output] Decoder log : Grants
[output] Event output : Per-call WAVs

Device --iq--> Trunk system
Trunk system --audio--> Speaker
Trunk system --events--> Decoder log
Trunk system --events--> Event output
```

| Protocol | Channel plan source |
|---|---|
| DMR Tier III / Capacity Max, P25 | Control channel broadcasts |
| DMR Capacity Plus, Hytera XPT | **Search** (carriers following the rest channel) |
| EDACS, LTR | Manual plan table (LCN or repeater number; LTR takes any repeater under **Control**; EDACS extended/ESK needs a standalone EDACS channel) |
| MPT 1327 | **Band** (`Ch 0 + N × spacing`) or plan table |

- **P25 TDMA** grants automatically spawn P25 Phase 2 on the granted slot.
- **Priority** preempts busy receivers, **Lockout** skips talkgroups, **Only these** restricts to priority list. Control failover is automatic.
- **Names** label talkgroups on the face and in the call log. Priority and Lockout take names too.
- Each receiver shows `talkgroup ← source`: green while the call is live, faded once idle.

## Voice privacy

Enter `key ID` and hex key under **Keys** (on Trunk system: `key ID:hex key`). Key length selects the cipher:

| Decoder | Hex digits |
|---|---|
| DMR | `10` ARC4, `32` AES-128, `64` AES-256 (Motorola Basic Privacy auto-recovers from first silence frame) |
| P25 Phase 1 | `10` ADP, `16` DES-OFB, `32` AES-128, `64` AES-256 |
| NXDN | `<= 4` scrambler, `16` DES-OFB, `64` AES-256 |

Late-entry DMR calls decrypt after two superframes if one key fits. Unmatched encrypted calls stay muted.

## Vocoder chip

Software voice uses `blip25`. Builds with `--features dvsi` support USB DVSI AMBE-3000 (1 ch) and AMBE-3003 (3 ch) dongles (460800 or 921600 baud): select the serial port under **Vocoder**. Busy or unresponsive chips fall back to `blip25`.
